entries.title: Love and weddings
q: how do i court a villager
entries.answer: Folk walk out, then marry in the chapel (or the square) the next evening. You can court and marry a folk too, all from the talk screen.
more: Two folk fond of each other walk out first: a walk together each evening, and a flower picked on the way. After two walks they are ready, and one asks the other at the end of a walk.

The wedding is dressed for what the town has: wildflowers and candles in a poor town; a carpet, flowers in pots, lanterns and banners in a middling one; an arch of flowers, coloured glass, a feast table and music in a rich one. A folk puts it all up that afternoon from the stores, the couple pay for it, and it comes down the morning after.
The guests sit, the officiant leads the vows, then the rings, a kiss, petals and the bell, a reception, and the couple walk out together.
Courting a folk yourself: it must be grown, unmarried, like you, and the town must respect you (Accepted or better).
tips: The town's news and the Families page say who is walking out with whom.
A widow or widower may love and marry again.
steps: Talk to the folk: About, Home, then 'Walk out with me?'.
Then 'Take a walk' (once a day, twice in all), 'Supper tonight?' (five coins) and give it a present. Each reply shows how fond it is.
When it is fond enough, 'Will you marry me?' asks properly; say it twice to confirm. The wedding is the next evening; be there.
Wed, it moves in by your bed, keeps its own work and greets you as its spouse ('How was your day?').
controls: [Right-click] a folk → About → Home → Walk out with me? · Take a walk · Supper tonight? · Will you marry me?

entries.title: Children and godparents
entries.answer: Couples have children when the town has room and food; children play, go to school and to a parent's side at work, and grow up in three days. You can have children with your spouse.
more: For three days it plays (tag, trailing its parents, exploring), goes to school, then grows up and takes a trade.
A friend of the town can ask a child 'Be godparent': it thinks the world of you, and its parents the better of you.
With a spouse, ask 'Try for a baby?'. That night, home asleep in the same house, hearts show over the bed. Soon after, your spouse says you are expecting and puts a crib up by the bed.

A few days later the child is born at home, with the healer there and the bell rung, and you name it ('Name the baby', said twice to confirm). It grows from baby to child to youngster to grown, and your page shows its schooling.
controls: [Right-click] a child → About → Home & pet → Be godparent
[Right-click] your spouse → About → Home → Try for a baby? · Name the baby
tips: Ask a child about itself and it says what it'll be when it grows up.
A child born into a full house gets a bed its parents buy at the shop.

entries.title: Households, homes and beds
entries.answer: Every folk belongs to a household with a house of its own, rented from the town at first and bought later. The town's books' Homes page shows them.
more: Grown children move out when a house is free; a folk without a bed lodges in a spare one; the builders put up houses while anyone waits.
controls: Town's books → People → Homes
[Right-click] a folk → About → Home & pet → Your home?
tips: A house shows who lives in it: its trade's things and luxuries (rugs, paintings, quilts), furnished out of ten.

entries.title: Pets: dogs and cats
q: how do i get a pet
entries.answer: Households keep dogs and cats. Right-click a pet with a Pet Treat to befriend it, or a stray to adopt it.
more: Right-click a household's pet with a Pet Treat to befriend it (two treats and it's your friend); right-click a stray with a treat to adopt it; or buy a pup or kitten from a litter (3 coins) by holding coins and right-clicking it.
controls: [Right-click] a pet with a Pet Treat
[Right-click] a folk → About → Home & pet → Your pet?
tips: Recipes: Pet Treat (2 wheat and a meat or fish, makes 4), Pet Bowl (planks, a bowl, planks; or 5 bricks for 2), Dog Bed (wool in 5 planks), Cat Basket (wool in 5 sticks), Pet Collar (string, leather, string; dye it like leather armour).
Place a bowl or bed in a folk's house and the household uses it.

entries.title: Fashion and clothes
q: can i give clothes to villagers
entries.answer: Folk dress up off work in coats, hats and scarves, and fashions sweep through the town. Ask any folk 'Fashion?'.
more: Over its trade's clothes a folk wears what it bought, was given or won: a long coat, leather jacket, shawl or waistcoat, a felt hat, flat cap or top hat off work, a scarf, a brooch, a rosette.
Fashions sweep through: a colour and a garment set by those the town looks up to, made by the tailor, and soon most of the town wears it.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Chat → More chat → Fashion?
Town's books → Culture → Fashion
tips: Hand a folk a garment (Give) and it puts it on there and then.
Every garment but the brooch can be dyed in a crafting grid, like leather armour.

entries.title: Health, healers and the infirmary
entries.answer: Folk catch colds that slow them for a day or two; the healer and infirmary see to them. If you're hurt, ask the healer 'See to me'.
more: Folk catch colds out in the rain or worked to the bone; a cold halves their pace for a day or two and never kills.
A Stone Age town of twenty builds an infirmary; its healer sees to the sick.
controls: [Right-click] the healer → Trade → Services → See to me
tips: Bandages (2 paper and a string, or a wool and 2 string, make 3) are the watch's and cave team's kit.
Herbal tea (sweet berries or a small flower, sugar, a water bottle) is a cup for a cold.

entries.title: Old age, deaths and vigils
entries.answer: Folk grow old and die in time, and the town holds a quiet vigil the evening after.
more: The evening after a death the town gathers quietly at the heart for a vigil, and those close grieve for a while.
The chronicle remembers everyone.
controls: Town's books → People (lifespans)
tips: Old folk with poor eyes are delighted by Spectacles.

entries.title: School, library and learning
entries.answer: Children go to school each morning, and the town's library lends real books. The town's books show both.
more: Children go to school each morning (a schoolteacher, desks, a blackboard; Slate and Chalk helps them learn a quarter faster).
The town library keeps a catalogue of real books by its writers and lends them; the store buys written books for it.
In class the teacher points at the board while the children write on their slates and put their hands up; after the lesson they play in the yard, then go on to their afternoon and home.
No school or no teacher yet: the children are taught at home of a morning, by a retired folk or a parent. No school on the day of rest.
Grown folk who went to school start their trade further on; the Apprentices page shows how many of the town's grown folk were schooled.
controls: Town's books → People → School
Town's books → Culture → Library

entries.title: The museum
entries.answer: The museum shows the town's rare finds and counts toward its renown. The town store buys finds it hasn't got.
more: The museum shows the town's rare finds (gems, discs, templates, a nether star...) and the first of each invention's working model; what it shows counts toward the town's renown.
controls: Town's books → Culture → Museum
Store counter → Sell (finds)

entries.title: Eating out: café, tavern, restaurant, inn
q: how do i eat at the restaurant
entries.answer: Sit at a table in the café, tavern or restaurant (right-click a chair) and the order screen opens. The waiter brings your food.
more: At a tavern ask the barkeep for a pint or a round; at an inn, a room for the night.
controls: [Right-click] a chair or table cloth → order screen
Barkeep → Trade → Shop → A pint · Buy a round · Bottles back
Innkeeper → A room for the night
tips: A plate and cup of your own (bricks and clay) can be set on a table too.
Each town has a local dish, marked on the card.

entries.title: Culture: banner, customs, arms
entries.answer: Each town has its own banner, arms, motto, customs and local dish. The town's books' Culture page shows them.
more: The village board flies its banner; citizens are given it.
controls: Town's books → Culture → Culture · Perks

entries.title: Seasons, weather, fire and drought
entries.answer: A town's year has four seasons of a week each, changing its fields and festivals. Fires, floods and droughts happen too.
more: The year turns through seasons that change what's grown, eaten and worn, with festivals in each.
Towns face fires, floods and droughts too: the folk fight fires with buckets and rain barrels, and the News page records it.
controls: Town's books → Overview (the season) · News

entries.title: Family trees and generations
q: what happens when a villager gets old
entries.answer: Each town keeps its family trees on the board's Families page. Old folk hand their trade to a grown child or their journeyman and retire; a house passes to the children.
more: At sixty-six a folk with an heir hands over its post and ground, and a knack for the trade, and retires: it watches its heir work of a morning and sits in the square of an afternoon.
A folk who dies with its trade in hand leaves it to its heir; the house stays with the household, and to the grown children when both parents are gone.
The town only has children while there is room, and builds houses for households waiting for one.
controls: Town's books → People → Families
[Right-click] a folk → its profile → Life
tips: A folk's profile shows its parents, partner, children, whom it is walking out with and what it came into.

entries.title: The week and the weekend
q: what day of the week is it
what do folk do at weekends
entries.answer: Every town keeps a seven-day week: Monday to Friday work, Saturday market day with most works shut, Sunday the day of rest.
more: The day of the week is at the top of your screen and on the town's board.

On Saturday folk have the day to themselves. They wander the town, buy things for themselves with their own money (a cake, a cap, a toy for their child, a drink at the tavern), and anyone with something spare sets up a stall in the square.
The fourth Saturday of each month the square fills with stalls, and traders walk in from the neighbouring towns with goods of their own. There is music, and races across the square.
Sunday: the service in the morning, games and football after, and walking out in the afternoon.
A young town (still in the Wood Age, or in its first week) works every day.
steps: Ask any folk 'What's on this week?' to open the week page.
The first tab lays out the next seven days and what is on each.
Press Show me on a day to get an arrow to the square, the chapel or the green.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Town → The week → What's on this week?
tips: Shops and the tavern stay open on Saturday, so that is the busiest day to sell.
Each folk's card shows what it did lately and why.

entries.title: Opening days and working hours
q: why are the farmers not working on saturday
entries.answer: Every employer has its own days and hours, and its hands work only those. A folk owner chooses by its character; you set your own business's on the week page.
more: An ambitious owner keeps long hours and opens every day; a hardworking one six days; an easygoing one four days, or short ones.
The town's own works keep the council's week, Monday to Friday. Shops, the market and the tavern open on Saturday.
An easygoing hand turns up an hour late; an ambitious one takes the Saturday morning's extra work when its employer offers it.
steps: Open the week page (ask a folk 'What's on this week?').
Go to the Hours tab and press Change hours beside your business.
Pick its days, opening and closing hours, then press Save these hours.
controls: Week page → Hours → Change hours → Save these hours
tips: The button rests and says why if the business is not yours.

entries.title: Friend levels, dinners and best friends
q: a villager invited me to dinner
how do i accept a dinner invitation
entries.answer: Folk count each other, and you, as an acquaintance, a friend, a close friend or a best friend. A folk who likes you well asks you to dinner at the weekend.
more: Friendship grows with chats, gifts, help, a dinner and a club night. Neighbours drop round on their days off, and friends ask each other to dinner at midday on a Saturday or Sunday.

An invitation goes on your planner with a toast. Be at the host's house around noon on the day: you sit down to whatever they have in, and they think the better of you. Saying yes and not coming is remembered.
A couple's best friends stand with them at their wedding and give the toast, and a baby's parents' best friends stand at the font at its christening.
steps: Talk to the folk who asked you and choose Accept dinner or Decline dinner.
On the day, go to their house around noon (Show me on the week page's Friends tab marks it).
controls: [Right-click] the host → Accept dinner / Decline dinner
Week page → Friends
tips: The Friends tab lists who in town counts you a friend, and how close.

entries.title: The Sunday service, christenings and funerals
entries.answer: The chaplain takes a short service every Sunday morning for those who go. Babies are christened the Sunday after they are born, and the dead have a funeral and a wake.
more: The devout always go; the rest as their character takes them. The chaplain stands at the front and gives a short sermon; the hymn is played on the harp between the lines.

A christening is straight after the service, at the chapel's font (or the well): the parents, the grandparents and the parents' best friends stand round. Your own child is christened too, and it goes on your planner.
A funeral is the morning after a death: the mourners gather at the chapel, walk behind the chaplain to the graveyard, the words are said and the stone set. Then the wake at the tavern.
Couples mark their wedding anniversary with a meal out together.
steps: Check the week page's Events tab for christenings and funerals coming.
Press Show me to get an arrow to the chapel.
controls: Week page → Events → Show me
tips: Every funeral and christening of folk you know goes on your planner.

entries.title: Clubs: fishing, choir, quiz, team and ramblers
q: how do i join a club
village team match on the green
entries.answer: The town has a fishing club, a choir, a pub quiz, a sports team and the ramblers. Folk join by what they are like, and you can join any of them.
more: The fishing club meets on Saturday morning at the water; the choir on Thursday evening at the chapel; the quiz on Friday evening at the tavern; the team trains on Wednesday evening and plays a match on Saturday afternoon on the green, with the town watching; the ramblers walk on Sunday afternoon.
A club needs a few members and somewhere to meet (water for the anglers, a tavern for the quiz). The page says why one cannot meet.
Members who turn up are the better friends for it, and remember a good meeting.
steps: Open the week page and go to the Clubs tab.
Press Join beside a club; its next meeting goes on your planner.
Turn up at its meeting place (Show me marks it).
controls: Week page → Clubs → Join
[Right-click] a member → Town → The week → Join their club
tips: Leave any time with the Leave button.
